claims: The Ivy League consists of eight private northeastern U.S. universities.
The Ivy League universities compete in NCAA Division 1 athletics.
The Ivy League schools are Brown, Columbia, Cornell, Dartmouth, Harvard, Penn, Princeton, and Yale.
Brown University is in Providence, RI.
Columbia University is in New York, NY.
Cornell University is in Ithaca, NY.
Dartmouth College is in Hanover, NH.
Harvard University is in Cambridge, MA.
University of Pennsylvania is in Philadelphia, PA.
Princeton University is in Princeton, NJ.
Yale University is in New Haven, CT.
Harvard's admission rate as of 2025-2026 is 3.6%.
Yale's admission rate as of 2025-2026 is 4.59%.
Princeton's admission rate as of 2025-2026 is 4.4%.
The term Ivy League originally referred to the athletic conference founded in 1954.
All Ivy League schools are located in the northeastern U.S.
